root_cause.text: The btrfs set received ioctl updated subvolume metadata inside a transaction before validating that adding the subvolume ID to the UUID tree’s BTRFS_UUID_KEY_RECEIVED_SUBVOL item would fit within the maximum leaf item size, so a later -EOVERFLOW in btrfs_uuid_tree_add() forced a transaction abort and remounted the filesystem read-only.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states “we did some metadata updates before” and therefore “have to abort the transaction” when adding BTRFS_UUID_KEY_RECEIVED_SUBVOL overflows; the patch fixes this by moving an early btrfs_uuid_tree_check_overflow() call before starting the transaction, with comments explicitly saying that without this check “the btrfs_uuid_tree_add() call below would fail with -EOVERFLOW and result in a transaction abort.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a pre-check for received UUID tree overflow so changing a subvolume's received UUID fails early instead of aborting the transaction and risking read-only filesystem state.
intent_record.what: The change introduces a new boolean-like check by assigning `received_uuid_changed = memcmp(root_item->received_uuid, sa->uuid, BTRFS_UUID_SIZE);` and adds a conditional block before the transaction work that, when the received UUID differs and the new UUID is not empty, calls `btrfs_uuid_tree_check_overflow(fs_info, sa->uuid, BTRFS_UUID_KEY_RECEIVED_SUBVOL)` and exits via `goto out` if it returns an error.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this pre-validates whether adding the new received UUID entry to the UUID tree would exceed the maximum item size before attempting the update. It prevents the later UUID-tree insertion path from failing with `-EOVERFLOW` inside a transaction, which would otherwise abort the transaction and could force the filesystem into read-only mode.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the local recomputation of received_uuid_changed so the subsequent UUID-update logic uses an already determined value.
intent_record.what: The assignment that computed received_uuid_changed by calling memcmp(root_item->received_uuid, sa->uuid, BTRFS_UUID_SIZE) was removed from this location, while subsequent logic still checks received_uuid_changed in the following if statement.
intent_record.how: This stops recalculating received_uuid_changed at that point, implying the value must now come from earlier code; at runtime, the later conditional behavior depends on a previously established value instead of recomputing it here.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a UUID tree overflow check that rejects appending another root ID when the existing item would exceed the leaf size limit.
intent_record.what: A new function, btrfs_uuid_tree_check_overflow(struct btrfs_fs_info *fs_info, const u8 *uuid, u8 type), was added. It validates that fs_info->uuid_root exists, allocates a btrfs path, builds a UUID tree key, searches the UUID tree for that key, returns success if the key does not exist, and if it does exist reads the current item size and compares sizeof(struct btrfs_item) + item_size + sizeof(u64) against BTRFS_LEAF_DATA_SIZE(fs_info), returning -EOVERFLOW when adding another u64 root ID would exceed the leaf item size limit.
intent_record.how: At runtime this provides a pre-insertion capacity check for UUID tree entries, allowing callers to detect in advance whether appending one more root ID to an existing UUID item would exceed the maximum space allowed in a leaf. It prevents attempts to grow an existing UUID tree item beyond the supported size and also rejects use when the UUID root is missing or path allocation fails.

intent_record.intent_summary: Export a UUID tree overflow-check helper so other code can detect or handle UUID tree overflow conditions.
intent_record.what: A new function declaration, `int btrfs_uuid_tree_check_overflow(struct btrfs_fs_info *fs_info, const u8 *uuid, u8 type);`, was added to the header alongside the existing UUID tree API declarations.
intent_record.how: This exposes a UUID tree overflow-checking function to other compilation units, enabling callers to invoke logic that detects or handles overflow conditions for a given UUID and type at runtime.

grouping_result.intent: Add a UUID tree overflow check that rejects appending another root ID when the existing item would exceed the leaf size limit.
Remove the local recomputation of received_uuid_changed so the subsequent UUID-update logic uses an already determined value.
Export a UUID tree overflow-check helper so other code can detect or handle UUID tree overflow conditions.

consistency_review.core_intent: Add early guard checks in UUID tree update paths to detect item growth overflow before modifying metadata, so the operation fails cleanly instead of causing transaction aborts or invalid leaf growth.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly target the root cause: they add early size/overflow validation in the UUID tree update path before metadata changes, preventing the later -EOVERFLOW in btrfs_uuid_tree_add() that would otherwise abort the transaction and remount the filesystem read-only.

The change only removes a local recomputation so later logic reuses an existing received_uuid_changed value. It does not add or move the missing UUID-tree size validation before transaction metadata updates, nor otherwise address the -EOVERFLOW/transaction-abort root cause.

The vulnerability is caused by UUID tree item size overflow being detected too late. Exporting a helper to check UUID tree overflow directly supports earlier validation/handling of that exact condition, so it is tied to the root cause.

This is the only visible pre-fix executable statement in the UUID-tree hunk, but it does not itself embody the overflow bug. The actual vulnerable append/growth logic that lacked a max-item-size check is not shown in the provided lines.
